question: England lost perhaps half its people in 1348 and 1349. When did its population regain the level it had before?
answer: In the early 1600s, on most estimates. Plague kept returning every decade or so, and deaths outran births: England fell further, to around 2 million in the mid-1400s. Only under the early Stuarts did it pass its pre-plague level of roughly 4.5 to 5 million. Some villages never returned, surviving as bumps in fields.
move: One blow heals; a blow that keeps repeating sets a new normal.
trap: Expecting a rebound within a few generations, as after one blow.
source: Broadberry et al., British Economic Growth, 2015
reference: Broadberry, Campbell, Klein, Overton and van Leeuwen, British Economic Growth, 1270-1870, Cambridge University Press, 2015
